facts.statement: Fossils of Inguza predemersus were discovered in Late Pliocene rocks at a quarry in Langebaanweg, South Africa, dating to approximately 5 million years ago.
facts.quote: The known fossils specimens were found in Late Pliocene rocks in a quarry at Langebaanweg, South Africa, from about 5 million years ago.

facts.statement: Inguza predemersus was originally classified in the genus Spheniscus but was later moved to its own monotypic genus after a distinct tarsometatarsus was identified.
facts.quote: It was formerly placed in the genus Spheniscus and presumed to be a close relative of the African penguin, but after its well-distinct tarsometatarsus was found, it was moved into its present monotypic genus.

facts.statement: Inguza predemersus is an extinct species of penguin.
facts.quote: Inguza predemersus is an extinct species of penguin.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Inguza predemersus is close to modern penguins or represents a late survivor of an extinct lineage.
facts.quote: Alternatively, it might not be close to extant penguins (the Spheniscinae), but a late survivor of an extinct lineage.

facts.statement: The genus Inguza lived from the Tortonian to the Zanclean stages, between 11.63 and 3.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Zanclean (11.63 to 3.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Inguza belongs to the penguin family Spheniscidae.
Inguza predemersus is the type species of the genus Inguza.
